note: Baseline sha256 of https://stohlerroof.com/'s raw HTML (the D-174 bridge domain carrying a mandatory legal disclosure -- see the netlify-deploy-drift.py module docstring's NON-GIT SITE CHECK section). This site has no repo_url and no `main` to diff against, so this pinned hash IS the compare target -- a mismatch in a live run is CONTENT_CHANGED, not noise. IMPORTANT (found capturing this baseline on gh-1734): the value MUST be captured via the script's own fetch_url_content() / urllib fetch, never via `curl` -- Cloudflare (in front of stohlerroof.com) serves this script's fetch a different response than a bare `curl -s` request gets, so a curl-captured baseline mismatches the script's own live reads on every single run even with zero real content change (confirmed live 2026-09-07: curl -> a23918238b0e..., this script's fetch_url_content() -> d684bf424f74..., stable across 3 repeated calls). CAVEAT (PR #1779 refuter MINOR 3, gh-1734 fix-1): the original capture note attributed this to the plain User-Agent HEADER TEXT specifically; a refuter found that Python's urllib sending the literal string "curl/8.4.0" as its User-Agent STILL got the clean hash, while the real curl binary (identical header text) got the dirty one -- so the actual discriminator is more likely a TLS/HTTP client fingerprint (JA3-style), not the UA header's text. The operative guidance (capture via fetch_url_content(), never curl) is unaffected either way and still holds; the precise mechanism is flagged here as uncertain rather than restated as settled fact. This also means the design stays brittle to a future Cloudflare fingerprinting change that starts treating urllib differently too -- flagged for visibility, not fixed in this pass (the issue's closes-on does not require it, per the refuter). Updating expected_sha256 (and captured_at) is a deliberate, reviewed act for whenever the disclosure copy is intentionally revised -- capture the new value the same way, via fetch_url_content(), never via curl or a browser -- and never an automatic self-heal in response to a live mismatch. STORAGE FORMAT (gh-1734 fix-2, 2026-09-07): this field was briefly stored as expected_sha256_parts (four 16-char hex fragments joined at load time by _load_content_baseline() in netlify-deploy-drift.py) specifically to dodge scripts/credential-sweep.py's HEX_RUN_20 pattern, which flags a bare 20+ contiguous hex-char run. A fresh-context re-reviewer on PR #1779 called that a real, generalizable technique for defeating a credential-shape detector on real (non-test) fixture data -- landed for dispatch-scope convenience rather than through the sweep's own sanctioned escape hatch (the allowlist). fix-2 reverted the split/join mechanism entirely: this is once again a single plain 64-char literal, and scripts/credential-sweep-allowlist.txt now carries an explicit, reviewed `value:` entry for it (see that file), the same audited mechanism used for this repo's existing SRI-hash and commit-sha entries.
